task: Write one sentence of your own using the word duplicity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know duplicity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The novel's charm curdles once readers spot the narrator's duplicity: he mourns his brother in the public chapters and toasts his ruin in the private letters.
Dishonesty covers any straying from the truth, down to a fib about homework; duplicity is a heavier charge - a sustained double game.
Treachery goes past duplicity: the duplicitous keep two faces in play, while treachery is the moment the hidden face strikes and the trust is actually betrayed.

Deceit is any dishonesty meant to mislead, and a single lie is enough to earn the word. Duplicity is a bigger, longer project: deliberately running two opposite stories at once - one face for one audience, its reverse for another - and keeping both alive over time.

Double-dealing is working both sides of a bargain for your own gain - selling to one buyer while secretly promising another. It lives in deals and negotiations. Duplicity covers the same two-faced betrayal anywhere at all: friendships, families, teams, with no bargain on the table required.

Guile is sly cleverness - the con artist's craft of misdirection and charm, almost admired as a skill. Duplicity is less about cleverness than about structure: deliberately keeping two contradictory faces alive for different audiences, month after month. A trickster has guile; a double agent practices duplicity.

Duplicity is a formal accusation of sustained two-facedness; for a single lie, deceit or dishonesty is enough.
